title: To be, and the personal pronouns
goal: Conjugate είμαι in the present and past, and use the subject pronouns.

blocks.text: **είμαι** 'I am' is the one verb whose endings follow no pattern, so learn it as a block. It has only two tenses: present and past. Greek normally drops the subject pronoun because the verb ending already shows the person: **Είμαι κουρασμένος** 'I am tired'. Use εγώ, εσύ and the others only for emphasis or contrast: **Εγώ** είμαι εδώ, **εσύ** πού είσαι;

blocks.cite: Holton §6.7. Forms in brackets are optional; slashes show equal alternatives.

blocks.text: **εσείς** is also the polite 'you' for one person: Πώς είστε; 'How are you?' to a stranger, Τι κάνεις; to a friend. The predicate stays in the nominative: Ο Γιάννης είναι **δάσκαλος**.

blocks.title: Από πού είσαι;
blocks.text: **Από πού είσαι;** 'Where are you from?' comes early in any Greek conversation, and the answer is often not where you live. Many Athenians are 'from' a family village or island: **Είμαι από την Κρήτη** for someone born in Athens to Cretan parents. Regional identity matters, and people say so with είμαι plus a demonym: **Είμαι Κρητικός**, **Είμαστε Μανιάτες**. At Easter and around 15 August (**Δεκαπενταύγουστος**) cities empty as people go **στο χωριό** 'to the village'.

items.why: χθες 'yesterday' needs the past; Νίκο is one person you know, so εσύ.
Polite plural for a person you address formally.
3rd singular and plural are the same: είναι.
An emphatic subject pronoun is nominative: εγώ.
After είμαι the predicate stays in the nominative.
χθες needs the past; 1st person plural ήμασταν/ήμαστε.
3rd person past, singular and plural alike: ήταν.

items.prompt: To your boss: ___ κουρασμένος, κύριε Νικολάου;
items.why: Polite address to one person uses the plural είστε.
3rd person singular: είναι.
A predicate adjective agrees with the subject in gender: feminine -η.
Predicate nominative plural: φίλοι.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: *We are tired.* (men or mixed)
items.why: είμαστε + masculine plural adjective (mixed groups take the masculine).

items.prompt: Say in Greek to a friend: *Where were you yesterday?*
items.why: 2nd singular past: ήσουν(α).

items.prompt: Say in Greek: *I am from Greece.*
items.why: από takes the accusative, with the article before country names.

items.prompt: Η Άννα και ο Πέτρος ___ φίλοι. (present)
items.why: 3rd person plural present: είναι, the same as the singular.

items.prompt: Χθες ___ στο σπίτι όλη μέρα. (εγώ, past)
items.why: 1st singular past: ήμουν(α).
2nd plural past: ήσασταν/ήσαστε.

items.prompt: Say politely to a man you don't know: *Are you Greek?*
items.why: Polite είστε, with a singular predicate because it is one person.
3rd singular past: ήταν(ε).

items.prompt: Say in Greek: *She is a teacher.* (primary school)
items.why: Pronoun dropped; feminine noun δασκάλα in the nominative.

items.prompt: Say in Greek (a man speaking): *I am not ill.*
items.why: δεν before the verb; predicate adjective in the nominative.

items.prompt: Say in Greek to a friend: *Are you here?*
items.why: 2nd singular είσαι; a question needs only intonation and ;.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: *We were students.* (mixed group, ο φοιτητής)
items.why: 1st plural past ήμασταν/ήμαστε; plural of φοιτητής is φοιτητές.
